_about.authoredOrGenerated: GENERATED by scripts/build-catalog.mjs — never edit by hand. Deterministic (content-hashed); `node scripts/build-catalog.mjs --check` fails CI if it is stale. Any edit to a contract's top-level description/version, or to a token file, requires regenerating catalog/ in the same commit.
_about.purpose: THE CONSUMER AGENT'S ENTRY POINT. An agent generating designs or code with UIDS starts at catalog.json and follows its readingOrder. The catalog deliberately LINKS to the authored sources (contracts) rather than restating them — with one exception: the token inventory, which it fully resolves so agents don't have to join three tiers of aliases themselves.

audiences.consumer agent: primary. catalog.json tells it what components/options/tokens legitimately exist; tokens.lean.json gives resolved values. This pair plus contracts/rules.json is everything a page-building agent needs.
audiences.builder agent: secondary — uses it as the compiled view the checkers diff against; edits SOURCES (tokens/, contracts/), never this.
audiences.checkers: check-figma.mjs reads the token inventory (resolved/px/ref/breakpoints) as its expectation of what Figma variables must hold. It is the only checker that consumes the catalog's CONTENT — build-catalog.mjs --check only re-emits and compares.
audiences.human: tokens.json (the WITH-provenance twin) is for humans tracing why a token holds its value.

_about.leanVsFull: tokens.lean.json and tokens.json carry the SAME 715 tokens and values. lean drops the per-token note/source provenance: ~66k -> ~30k model tokens per load. HAND AN AGENT THE LEAN ONE; the full one is for provenance questions only. Both are emitted every build so they cannot drift apart.
moreInfo: contracts/README.md — 'The agent catalog (catalog/)' section: what the catalog holds and why it links instead of restating
scripts/build-catalog.mjs — header documents determinism and the --check gate
docs/examples/tokens.example.json — the AUTHORED token format this inventory is compiled from

catalog.json.description_readingOrder: What the catalog is + the ordered list of what a consumer agent should read (rules first, then the relevant contract, then tokens.lean.json).
catalog.json.rules_tokens_tokensWithProvenance_figmaF: Pointers: the governance rules file, the two token inventories, the Figma library URL, and the regeneration command.

components[].id_name_version_description: id, version and description are copied from the contract — so a description or version edit stalens the catalog. `name` is NOT a copy: build-catalog.mjs:120 sets it to identity.figma.componentSetName ?? contract.name, so it is usually the Figma set's display name. Live divergences: badge -> "Badge", accordion -> "Accordion Item", background -> "background". Corollary worth knowing: editing identity.figma.componentSetName also stalens the catalog, not just the Figma snapshot.
components[].contract_code_storybook: LINKS to the authored contract, the Vue/SCSS source, and the Storybook id — the catalog sends you there rather than restating shape.
components[].figma: componentSetId / componentKey / page anchors into the library.
components[].options: Option NAMES only — the values, defaults, and slots live in the linked contract.
components[].tokens: This component's tokensUsed list, verbatim — the names to look up in tokens.lean.json.

tokens.lean.json.topLevel: description, count, omittedFields (what lean dropped), provenance (where to find it), tokens{}

perTokenEntry.value: the authored value or {alias.reference} exactly as written in tokens/
perTokenEntry.resolved: the alias-chain-resolved CSS value (e.g. '0.75rem') — what actually renders
perTokenEntry.px: the same value in px — but ONLY for rem values: build-catalog.mjs:81-84 matches /^([\d.]+)rem$/, so em, %, keyword and multi-part values get NO px key at all. Verify before relying on it: catalog/tokens.lean.json['badge/padding/inline'] is {tier, value: '.75em', resolved: '.75em'} with no px. The bare-em subtlety (an em resolves against the OWNING COMPONENT's font-size, not 16) is check-figma.mjs behaviour via its emBasis/pxOf helpers — it is not reflected here.
perTokenEntry.ref: the Figma variable this token aliases to, when it is an alias (e.g. 'font/size/25')
perTokenEntry.breakpoints: present only when the token switches per mode: the per-breakpoint values for mobile / md (980) / page (1350)

extraFields.note: the authored comment — provenance, rulings, and traps (e.g. WHY badge/font-size is absolute). This is the ~36k tokens the lean file saves.

badge/font-size.note: badge.scss:8. CHANGED 2026-08-20 from a raw 75% to an absolute rem primitive, per the design system owner's ruling… (full text in the real file)
